title: SYSTEM BOOT — SEQUENCE INITIALIZATION
body:
>> DHARMA INITIATIVE ORIENTATION SYSTEM — ONLINE
>> STATION: THE SWAN (STATION 3 OF 6)
>> OPERATIVE STATUS: ACTIVE

You are now the sole operator of this station.

Your mission is simple. Every 108 minutes, you will enter the sequence. You will not ask why. You will not attempt to leave. The work is important. The work is necessary.

4   8   15   16   23   42

Enter the numbers. Push the button.
Do not let the counter reach zero.

title: Observations on the Nature of the Experiment
subtitle: Being a record of what was seen, and what was not meant to be seen
body:
The Pearl station was designed as an observation post. Monitors, notebooks, pneumatic tubes. We were told we were watching the watchers — behavioral scientists logging the psychological toll of meaningless labor.

What they did not tell us is that every tube led nowhere. The notebooks were incinerated. The observation was not the work. We were the experiment.

I have come to believe that everything on this island is a mirror. What you look at looks back. The man in the hatch below is no less free than we are. He has his button. We have our notebooks. Neither of us knows what truly happens when we complete the task.
footer: — Dr. Marvin Candle, Internal Memorandum, NEVER TO BE DISTRIBUTED

title: Inventory of the Dead
subtitle: A partial accounting, recovered from the storage bunker
body:
What remains after the purge is not nothing. It is everything that was left behind.

In the Arrow station, they stored what could not be carried — the objects of the departed. A glass eye, wrapped in cloth. A radio transmitter, batteries long dead. Personal effects cataloged with the clinical detachment of those who believed documentation was a form of mercy.

But mercy for whom?

The island does not forget. Its soil absorbs what is buried in it. The bones of the DHARMA scientists rest in the same earth as those who put them there. In time, the jungle will take back the stations too. Canvas and corrugated metal are no match for something that has been growing for four hundred years.

We are all inventory here.
footer: SOURCE: Recovered Notebook, Arrow Station. Author Unknown.

title: On the Properties of the Frozen Wheel
subtitle: A theoretical framework for understanding the island's temporal mechanics
body:
The wheel was not built. It was discovered.

This distinction matters enormously and has been deliberately obscured in all official DHARMA documentation. The chamber below the Orchid predates our arrival by an indeterminate span. The wheel was already there, set into bedrock, already aligned with the electromagnetic pocket beneath it.

Somebody, in some other time, understood what this island was capable of.

Our research suggests the wheel functions as a kind of valve — a mechanical interface between the island's electromagnetic properties and something else. Something we lack language to describe properly. Not a place. Not a time. A state.

I believe the island is alive. Not metaphorically. I mean this in the most literal sense of which science is capable.

Turning the wheel moves the island through that state. The operative is displaced. The island is not.
footer: — Benjamin Linus, Research Summary (Unofficial). This document does not exist.

title: Case File: Patient Zero of the Sickness
subtitle: Medical records, Station Staff, Classified
body:
She came to us from the jungle on a Tuesday, or what we believe was a Tuesday. The island makes calendars feel presumptuous.

She was French. She was pregnant. She had already lost the others in her team, though she did not say how. Her eyes had the quality of someone who has seen something that reassembled the world into a shape she could not yet describe.

We delivered the child on a night of intense electrical activity — the instruments all spiked simultaneously, the lights went out. When they came back, the baby was healthy. The mother was not the same.

I have no clinical term for what I observed in the weeks after. The DHARMA manual calls it 'reactive environmental syndrome.' The other doctors call it 'the sickness.'

I call it what the jungle calls out of you when you stay too long.
footer: — Dr. Arzt, Medical Station Log (Recovered, Incomplete)

No transmission leaves or enters this island without passing through us first.

The code to disable the jamming signal is known to exactly one person. We were told this was a security measure. We have now been stationed here for four years. We have not been relieved.

title: What the Countdown Costs
subtitle: A meditation written in the margins of the Swan Orientation Manual
body:
You push the button because you're afraid of what happens if you don't.

At first, you push it because they told you to. Then because the training said to. Then because Radzinsky said so, before Radzinsky was gone.

Then you push it because you've been down here so long that the button is the only ritual you have left. It marks time. It divides the formless dark into 108-minute increments of almost-purpose.

Then one day, maybe, you stop pushing it. Not because you've decided anything. Not because you're brave. But because you've pushed it so many times you've forgotten what the alternative feels like, and forgetting feels, in some exhausted way, like freedom.

That's when it matters most. That's when the clock means everything.

Push the button, Desmond.

Brother, please.
footer: — Found in the margins of the Swan Orientation Manual, handwriting unidentified
